environmentalPersistence: Low — atmospheric half-life ~1 hour via photolysis; in solution degrades within days

morphologicalEffects.heightSuppression: Moderate-strong — cell division inhibited by protein crosslinking
morphologicalEffects.leafCurl: Moderate — acute cellular damage causes curling
morphologicalEffects.necrosis: Strong — tissue death at point of contact; spreads inward from stomatal entry points
morphologicalEffects.pigmentation: Mild — some stress anthocyanin but overwhelmed by necrotic browning
morphologicalEffects.newVsOldLeaves: All leaves affected; young leaves with more open stomata more vulnerable

physiologyEffects.chlorophyllReduction: Strong — 50–70% at moderate exposure; direct protein denaturation
physiologyEffects.stomatalConductance: Strongly reduced — guard cell proteins damaged
physiologyEffects.membranePermeability: Strongly increased — crosslinking disrupts membrane proteins

molecularEffects.oxidativeStress: Strong — formaldehyde directly generates ROS and depletes glutathione

microbiomeEffects.diversityReduction: Strong — formaldehyde is a broad-spectrum biocide
microbiomeEffects.beneficialBacteriaEffect: Strongly suppressed — near sterilization at high doses

firstSymptoms: leaf surface bleaching/whitening at contact points
temporalDynamics.recoveryTime: Poor — protein crosslinking damage is permanent; only new growth recovers

visualSimulation.colorChanges: Green → bleached white/gray at contact points → brown necrosis; background yellowing
visualSimulation.firstAffectedRegion: Leaf surface at stomatal entry points
visualSimulation.damageSpread: Inward from leaf surface; acute exposure creates discrete bleached zones
visualSimulation.damagePattern: Patchy bleached/necrotic spots progressing to uniform damage
visualSimulation.heatmapGlow: Moderate red-orange glow — MDA and GSH depletion signature
visualSimulation.microbiomeParticles: Strongly reduced; near-zero diversity at high dose
visualSimulation.recoveryVisual: No recovery on affected tissue; only new growth post-exposure is healthy

synergies.synergyNote: Formaldehyde + other indoor VOC pollutants create additive to synergistic oxidative stress — shared GSH depletion mechanism overwhelms antioxidant capacity

educationalContext.realWorldSources: Pressed wood products, furniture, carpets, cigarette smoke, vehicle exhaust, building materials — major indoor air pollutant
educationalContext.agriculturalUse: Soil fumigant (historical); now largely banned for agricultural use
educationalContext.humanToxicity: High — IARC Group 1 carcinogen; causes nasopharyngeal cancer; irritant at low concentrations
educationalContext.climateLink: Formed as secondary pollutant from methane and other VOC oxidation in atmosphere
educationalContext.indoorOutdoor: Primarily indoor — off-gassing from furniture and building materials; major sick building syndrome component
educationalContext.whyStudentsCare: Present in most classrooms and homes via furniture and building materials — directly relevant to indoor air quality and personal health
educationalContext.realWorldIssue: Indoor air quality, sick building syndrome, occupational health, VOC regulation
